preamble: Languages borrowing from French regularly replace the French uvular rhotic /ʁ/ with their native coronal tap /ɾ/. Lahrouchi shows that Moroccan Arabic and Tashlhiyt Berber adapt French [ʁ] (and its devoiced variant [χ]) systematically as a tap even though both languages have native /ʁ/ and /χ/, and Turkish French loans likewise show /ɾ/ in place of [ʁ]. This is loanword substitution rather than an internal sound change.

examples.note: Produced by monolingual speakers with no access to French phonology; Lahrouchi transcribes the tap as r.
Cited by Lahrouchi as a form shared by Tashlhiyt Berber and Moroccan Arabic; the tap is pharyngealized here.

sources: Lahrouchi, M. (2019). Not as you R: Adapting the French rhotic into Arabic and Berber. LingBuzz 004422. https://ling.auf.net/lingbuzz/004422
